inferences: The production role tested here is bounded autonomy under continued human responsibility, not removal of the human service interface.
Aggregate speed gains can coexist with worse subjective experience in the tasks delegated to the agent.
A handoff mechanism alone is insufficient when the system recognizes emotional deterioration too late.
research_judgment: This is direct counterevidence to a simple interface-replacement or centralized-control-layer narrative. It shows real task execution and efficiency gains, but only within a narrow eligible subset and with material dependence on human supervision, monitoring quality and intervention timing. The evidence does not show that agents cannot become an interface or control layer; it narrows the conditions under which that transition is likely to work.

thesis_impacts.explanation: The tested agent handled a small standardized subset while humans retained completion responsibility, and customer ratings fell in AI-eligible chats despite faster service.
Reliability and emotional-recovery limits required task classification, algorithmic monitoring and timely human intervention, constraining an autonomous control-layer interpretation.

alternative_explanations: Lower ratings may reflect communication style rather than failure to resolve the issue.
The system was early and limited to less than 10% of chats; later models or better monitoring may improve both coverage and experience.
Customer service may be unusually sensitive to emotion and may not represent back-office workflows.
unknowns: The paper does not disclose software revenue, deployment cost or long-run labor demand.
The persistence of the measured effects after further model and workflow iteration is unknown.
The interface usage displaced by the agent is not measured.
follow_up_indicators: Track AI-eligible share, intervention rate and time-to-intervention in later deployments.
Track customer ratings and retrials separately from speed and containment.
Seek comparable randomized evidence outside customer service.
